getCriticalN performs a Monte Carlo simulation to estimate the number of times the most frequent taxon is expected to be observed in a list of signatures

Source: R/montecarlo.R
getCriticalN.Rd

getCriticalN performs a Monte Carlo simulation to estimate the number of times the most frequent taxon is expected to be observed in a list of signatures

Usage

getCriticalN(
  relevant.sigs,
  siglengths,
  alpha = 0.05,
  nsim = 1000,
  ci = 0.95,
  ci_nsim = 500
)

Arguments

relevant.sigs

a list of signatures that form the "background" from which taxa for simulated signatures will be drawn. These are used to estimate how frequently taxa occur

siglengths

The sizes of signatures found in a set of related studies. Simulated signatures will match these in number and size.

alpha

Probability at which a critical threshold will be calculated (default: 0.05)

nsim

Number of simulations (default: 1000)

ci

Width of the bootstrap confidence interval to compute around the critical threshold, e.g. 0.95 for a 95% CI (default: 0.95). Set to NULL to skip.

ci_nsim

Number of bootstrap resamples used to compute the CI (default: 500)

Value

A list: critical_n is the 1 - alpha quantile of simulated values for the maximum number of times any taxon is identified, ci_lower/ci_upper give the bootstrap CI around it (NA if ci = NULL), simulated_values holds the raw simulated maxima, plus alpha and a quantile_label for printing.

Details

E.g. for alpha = 0.05, we expect only a 5% chance that any taxon will be identified N times or more.

Examples

full.dat <- bugsigdbr::importBugSigDB()
#> Using cached version from 2026-11-09 16:28:46
my.dat <- full.dat[full.dat$Curator == "Mst Afroza Parvin", ]
relevant.dat <- full.dat[full.dat$`Body site` %in% my.dat$`Body site`, ]
relevant.sigs <- bugsigdbr::getSignatures(my.dat)
my.sigs.increased <- relevant.sigs[grep("UP", names(relevant.sigs))]
(my.siglengths <- sapply(my.sigs.increased, length))
